name: aggindex-minmax-allnull-group-dropped
tables: CREATE TABLE t (id BIGINT NOT NULL, g BIGINT, v BIGINT, PRIMARY KEY (id))
CREATE INDEX max_by_g AS SELECT MAX(v) FROM t GROUP BY g
CREATE INDEX min_by_g AS SELECT MIN(v) FROM t GROUP BY g

groups.name: max-allnull-group-kept
groups.reason: FIXED (was an engine bug): GROUP BY g yields a group for every distinct g present; g=2 has two rows (all v NULL) so MAX(v)=NULL and [2, NULL] MUST appear. `WHERE id IS NOT NULL` is a no-op (id is a NOT NULL PK), so the two queries select the identical rows and must yield the identical grouped result. Previously the index-backed MAX dropped the all-NULL group g=2 because SQL MAX wrongly mapped to a MAX_EVER_LONG index (which skips NULL values, so an all-NULL group has no index entry). Now SQL MAX maps to a PERMUTED_MAX index (matching Java's NumericAggregationValue.Max), which indexes the all-NULL group's NULL extremum, so both queries return [1,10],[2,NULL]. Regression sentinel: this equivalence must keep holding.
queries: SELECT g, MAX(v) FROM t GROUP BY g
SELECT g, MAX(v) FROM t WHERE id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY g

groups.name: min-allnull-group-kept
groups.reason: FIXED (was an engine bug): same as the MAX case for the MIN aggregate index. g=2 (all v NULL) must appear as [2, NULL]; SQL MIN now maps to a PERMUTED_MIN index (matching Java's NumericAggregationValue.Min) which keeps the all-NULL group, so index-backed and scan-backed MIN agree at [1,10],[2,NULL].
queries: SELECT g, MIN(v) FROM t GROUP BY g
SELECT g, MIN(v) FROM t WHERE id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY g
